look_here_first: For TALL goldenrod, inspect SHORT, FINE hairs low on a standing stem and a FIRM, often noticeably rough three-nerved middle leaf. Check if upper-mid leaves are entire or sparsely toothed. Compare Canada goldenrod: often thinner more serrated leaves and less crowded longer stem hairs — many characters overlap. Giant goldenrod tends to have genuinely smooth/waxy lower stem. Photograph the stem at ground level and the leaf UNDERSIDE, not only the yellow plume.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Tall erect herb often forming colonies.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Many very small yellow heads in arching or plume-like panicles.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: tall golden panicles; rough leaves/stems; colony-forming habit; If working below species level, do not assign a subspecies from general goldenrod habit alone; Joey's exact reference is S. altissima subsp. gilvocanescens.

key_traits.label: Joey reference note
key_traits.text: Joey's exact iNaturalist photo reference is Solidago altissima subsp. gilvocanescens. Use it as an infraspecific habit/morphology comparison, not as evidence that every local tall goldenrod belongs to that subspecies.
